entry: Fluid [[Distillation|distilled]] from the [[Resin|resin]] of living trees, mainly [[Pine|pines]]. Principally used as a specialized solvent, it is also a source of material for organic syntheses. It is composed of terpenes, primarily α-pinene and β-pinene, with lesser amounts of carene, camphene, [[Limonene]] and terpinolene. Nowadays it is rarely distilled from pine resin; most is a byproduct of pulping. The sulfite process yields a cymene-rich product, the kraft process a pinene-rich one. Substitutes include white spirit and other [[Petroleum|petroleum]] distillates, though their chemicals differ.

Opaque blue-to-green [[Mineral|mineral]], a hydrous phosphate of [[Copper|copper]] and aluminum, prized as a [[Gemstone|gemstone]] for millennia. The finest grades reach a Mohs hardness just under 6. The sky-blue color of Persian turquoise, mined near Nishapur, [[Iran]], has long served as a reference for quality. Like most opaque gems, it has been devalued by treatments, imitations and synthetics. Pre-Columbian Native Americans mined it in [[New Mexico]], and [[Ancient Egypt|Ancient Egyptians]] used it, though not commonly. The name derives from Old French *turquois*, "Turkish", although the mineral is not found in Turkey.

Species of small, biologically immortal [[Jellyfish|jellyfish]], also called the immortal jellyfish. Found worldwide in temperate to tropical waters, it is one of few known animals able to revert from the sexually mature medusa stage to a sedentary polyp colony. The reversal occurs through transdifferentiation, a process that changes existing cells into new types, and can be triggered by stress, injury or age. In theory it could repeat indefinitely, though in nature most individuals are likely to succumb to predation or disease first. Its capacity for biological immortality makes it an important target of research into aging and pharmaceuticals.

Reptile of the order *Testudines*, characterized by a shell developed mainly from its ribs. Turtles fall into two major groups, *Pleurodira* (side-necked turtles) and *Cryptodira* (hidden-necked turtles), which differ in how the head retracts. About 360 living or extinct species are known, including land-dwelling [[Tortoise|tortoises]] and freshwater terrapins. The domed carapace and flatter plastron form a shell made mostly of [[Bone|bone]] and covered in keratin scales. Turtles are ectothermic and generally opportunistic omnivores. [[Sea turtle|Sea turtles]] are the only reptiles that migrate long distances to lay eggs on a favored beach. The leatherback, the largest living species, can exceed 2.7 m (8 ft 10 in) in length. Many species are extinct or threatened because of hunting, bycatch in fishing nets and habitat destruction.

Region of central [[Italy]]. Its capital and largest city is [[Florence]]. Tuscany is regarded as the birthplace of the [[Renaissance|Italian Renaissance]] and of the foundations of the Italian language, which were shaped by the literature of [[Dante Alighieri]], [[Petrarch]], Giovanni Boccaccio, [[Niccolò Machiavelli]] and Francesco Guicciardini. Its museums include the [[Uffizi]] and the Palazzo Pitti, and its wines include Chianti and Brunello di Montalcino. The [[Etruscan civilization|Etruscans]] created the first major civilization in the region. Eight Tuscan localities are World Heritage Sites, including the historic centers of Florence, San Gimignano and Siena. The region has over 120 protected nature reserves. In 2018 Florence alone had over 5 million tourist arrivals.

Egyptian [[Pharaoh|pharaoh]] of the Eighteenth Dynasty (r. c. 1332–1323 BC). Born Tutankhaten, he restored the traditional polytheistic [[Ancient Egyptian religion|religion]] of ancient Egypt, reversing the Atenism of [[Akhenaten]]'s reign, and changed his name to Tutankhamun. He moved the royal court back to Memphis and reestablished diplomatic relations with the [[Mitanni]]. His military campaigns reached [[Nubia]] and the Near East. He died at about 19 and was buried in a small tomb, because his royal tomb in the [[Valley of the Kings]] was unfinished. Excavators led by Howard Carter discovered the tomb in 1922, which had been robbed in antiquity but retained much of its contents, including over 5,000 artifacts and the king's undisturbed mummy. His mask, preserved at the [[Egyptian Museum]], remains a popular symbol.

Republic of [[Russia]] at the geographical center of [[Asia]], in southern [[Siberia]]. Its 336,651 people (2021 census) are 88.7% ethnic Tuvan and 10.1% ethnic Russian. Chinese dynasties and nomadic khanates controlled the area before the [[Qing dynasty]] incorporated it in 1758 as part of Outer Mongolia. A Russian protectorate followed in 1914, under [[Nicholas II]]. The nominally independent Tuvan People's Republic, recognized only by the [[Soviet Union]] and Mongolia, was annexed into the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic in 1944. As of 2012, 61.8% adhered to [[Buddhism]] and 8% to [[Shamanism|Tuvan shamanism]].

Archipelagic island country in the [[Polynesia|Polynesian]] subregion of [[Oceania]], midway between Hawaii and Australia. It is composed of three reef islands and six atolls, lying west of the [[International Date Line]]. The 2022 census recorded 10,643 people, making it the second least populated member of the [[United Nations]]. Its first inhabitants, Polynesians, arrived as part of a migration that began about three thousand years ago. A British protectorate was proclaimed in 1892, and Tuvalu became a separate colony in 1976. It became fully independent on 1 October 1978, as a constitutional monarchy within the [[Commonwealth of Nations|Commonwealth]] with [[Charles III]] as king. With little soil, the country relies on fishing licenses, remittances and aid. Being low-lying, it is extremely vulnerable to [[Climate change|sea level rise]].

Major deities of the Greek pantheon, so named for their residence on [[Mount Olympus]]. The canonical number is twelve: [[Zeus]], Poseidon, Hera, Demeter, Aphrodite, [[Athena]], Artemis, [[Apollo]], Ares, Hephaestus, [[Hermes]], and either Hestia or [[Dionysus]]. Zeus led his siblings to victory over the [[Titans]] in the Titanomachy, establishing their supremacy. [[Hades]], brother of Zeus, was usually excluded because his realm lay in the underworld. Other cultic groupings of twelve gods existed across ancient Greece.

English model, actress and singer. She rose to fame as a teenage model in London's Swinging Sixties and became one of the first international supermodels. Named "The Face of 1966" by the *Daily Express*, she was known for her thin build, short hair and large eyes. She modeled in France, Japan and the [[United States]] before retiring temporarily in 1970. Her first leading role, in the musical *The Boy Friend* (1971), won her two Golden Globes. She made her Broadway debut in *My One and Only* (1983), earning a Tony nomination, and later judged *America's Next Top Model*.

Daylight illumination from diffuse sky radiation while the [[Sun]] is below the [[Horizon|horizon]], as sunlight from the upper atmosphere is scattered. The sky dims as the Sun sinks, and illumination is nearly zero when it reaches 18° below the horizon. Civil twilight, when the Sun's center is between the horizon and 6° below it, gives enough light that artificial light is unnecessary for most outdoor activity. Photographers and painters call it the blue hour, from the French *l'heure bleue*. Metaphorically, twilight implies something losing strength and nearing its end.

American surrealist mystery-horror television series created by [[David Lynch]] and Mark Frost. Set in the fictional [[Pacific Northwest]] town of Twin Peaks, Washington, it follows FBI agent Dale Cooper's investigation of the murder of local teenager Laura Palmer. It blends [[Detective fiction|detective fiction]], [[Soap opera|soap opera]] and horror. It ran on ABC from 1990 until its cancellation in 1991, and returned for a third season on Showtime in 2017. The prequel film *Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me* (1992) expanded its story. The series developed a devoted cult following and is often listed among the greatest television series of all time.

One of two offspring produced by the same [[Pregnancy|pregnancy]]. Identical, or monozygotic, twins develop from one zygote that splits into two [[Embryo|embryos]], and always share the same chromosomal sex. Fraternal, or dizygotic, twins develop from two separate eggs, each fertilized by its own sperm, and share on average 50 percent of their genes, like ordinary [[Sibling|siblings]]. Twin birth rates vary widely: the [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] have the highest, at 45–50 twin sets per 1,000 live births, while South America, South Asia and Southeast Asia have the lowest, at six to nine twin sets. Twin pregnancies last on average 37 weeks, three weeks less than full term. Fraternal twinning runs in families through the mother. Unrelated look-alikes are called [[Doppelgänger|doppelgängers]].

American video live-streaming service, popular for video game and [[Esports|esports]] broadcasts. Launched in June 2011 as a spin-off of the general-interest streaming site *Justin.tv*, it is operated by Twitch Interactive, a subsidiary of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]]. Amazon acquired it in August 2014 for US$970 million. Twitch had 45 million unique viewers in October 2013 and over 100 million viewers a month by 2015. It also carries music, creative content and "in real life" streams. In 2023 it announced it would stop operating in South Korea in 2024 because of network fees.

Composer of [[Carnatic music]], a form of [[Indian classical music]]. Along with his contemporaries [[Muthuswami Dikshitar]] and [[Syama Sastri]], he is regarded as the trinity of Carnatic music. Tyagaraja composed hundreds of devotional *kritis*, mostly in Telugu and in praise of [[Rama]], and many remain popular. His five compositions known as the *Pañcaratna Kṛti* are often sung in programs in his honor. He lived through the reigns of four kings of the Thanjavur Maratha rule, although he served none of them. He spent most of his life in Thiruvaiyaru, where the annual Tyagaraja Aradhana festival is held in his memory.

Danish astronomer, whose unprecedentedly accurate observations helped launch the [[Scientific Revolution]]. In 1572 he noticed a new star, now designated SN 1572, brighter than any star or planet, and he devoted the following years to more accurate instruments. His measurements showed that such [[Supernova|supernovae]] lay beyond the Moon and that comets were not atmospheric phenomena. King Frederick II gave him the island of Hven, where he built Uraniborg, the first large [[Observatory|observatory]] in Christian Europe. He devised the Tychonic system, in which the planets orbit the Sun while the Sun orbits the Earth. After King Christian IV forced him to leave Denmark in 1597, he became imperial astronomer in [[Prague]]. [[Johannes Kepler]], who later used Brahe's data to formulate his laws of planetary motion, assisted him for a year before his death.

American filmmaker and actor, creator of the character Madea. Born Emmitt Perry Jr., he wrote stage plays in the 1990s, and he created the elderly Mabel "Madea" Simmons. His breakthrough film, *Diary of a Mad Black Woman* (2005), adapted one of his plays. He developed *Tyler Perry's House of Payne*, which ran for eight seasons on TBS. In 2012 he signed an exclusive partnership with [[Oprah Winfrey]]. His films and shows have grossed over $660 million, and critics argue they perpetuate negative portrayals of [[African Americans]]. [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named him among the most influential people in 2020.

American actress, best known for her role as Detective Mary Beth Lacey. Born in [[Madison, Wisconsin|Madison]], Wisconsin, she has won six Emmy Awards and a Tony Award. She won four Emmys for playing Lacey in the [[CBS]] police drama *Cagney & Lacey* (1982–88), and she won further Emmys for *Christy* and *Judging Amy*. Her Broadway revival of *Gypsy* (1989) earned the Tony for Best Actress in a Musical. She played [[Maria Callas]] in *Master Class* on Broadway and in [[London]]'s West End. Her films include *The Enforcer* (1976) and *The Ballad of Buster Scruggs* (2018).

Mechanical or electromechanical machine for typing characters. Each key causes a type element to strike an [[Ink|inked]] ribbon against paper, producing a legible document. The first commercial typewriters appeared in 1874, but became common in U.S. offices only after the mid-1880s. By the end of the 19th century, a person who used one was also called a typist. Typewriters were standard office equipment until the 1980s, when personal computers running [[Word processor|word processing]] software largely replaced them. The typewriter was an early accessibility tool, and its use for the blind accelerated its development. The [[QWERTY]] layout, developed for typewriters in the 1870s, remains the de facto standard for English-language [[Computer keyboard|computer keyboards]]. Typewriters are still used in many [[India|Indian]] cities and towns, especially in roadside and legal offices, where electricity is unreliable.

[[Genus]] of about 30 species of [[Monocotyledon|monocotyledonous]] flowering plants in the family Typhaceae. Known as bulrushes, reedmaces or cattails depending on region, these aquatic or semiaquatic perennials grow to 0.8–2.4 m tall, with long, narrow leaves. They are largely distributed across the Northern Hemisphere, in [[Wetland|wetland]] habitats. They colonize newly exposed mud from wind-dispersed seeds and spread by rhizomes into dense stands that often exclude other plants. In North America they have displaced native sedges and wet meadows. Many parts are edible, including the [[Starch|starchy]] rhizomes, though plants can accumulate toxins in polluted areas. When ripe, the heads disintegrate into cottony fluff that carries the seeds on the wind.

Enteric disease caused by the bacterium [[Salmonella]] Typhi, spread through food or water contaminated with feces. Symptoms usually begin six to 30 days after exposure, with a gradual onset of high fever, weakness, abdominal pain, constipation and headache. Some people develop a rash with rose-colored spots, and others carry the bacterium without symptoms while remaining contagious. Diagnosis is by culturing *S. Typhi* from patient samples or detecting an immune response in blood. A [[Vaccination|vaccine]] can prevent about 40–90% of cases during the first two years, and antibiotics such as azithromycin are used, though resistance has developed. Untreated, the risk of death may be as high as 20%, and with treatment 1% to 4%. In 2015 about 149,000 people died of typhoid worldwide, down from 181,000 in 1990. Its name means *resembling [[Typhus|typhus]]*, a different disease.

[[Tropical cyclone]] producing sustained hurricane-force winds of at least 119 km/h (74 mph) in the northwestern Pacific. The region accounts for almost one-third of the world's tropical cyclones. From 1950 to 2022 it averaged 26.5 named tropical cyclones a year, of which 16.6 reached typhoon standard. The Philippines receive most landfalls, but some of the deadliest typhoons have struck [[China]]. Taiwan has recorded the wettest known typhoon in the basin. Vietnam's typhoon season runs from June through November, with four to six typhoons hitting the country annually.

Group of bacterial infectious diseases, including epidemic, scrub and murine typhus. Epidemic typhus, caused by *Rickettsia prowazekii* and spread by body lice, occurs in outbreaks where sanitation is poor and people are crowded. Scrub typhus, caused by *Orientia tsutsugamushi* and spread by chiggers, occurs in [[Southeast Asia]], Japan and northern Australia. Murine typhus, caused by *Rickettsia typhi* and spread by [[Flea|fleas]], occurs in tropical and subtropical areas. Symptoms include fever, headache and a rash one to two weeks after exposure. Treatment is with [[Doxycycline]], and no [[Vaccine|vaccine]] is commercially available. Described since at least 1528, the name comes from the Greek *tûphos*, meaning *hazy* or *smoky*. It is distinct from [[Typhoid fever|typhoid fever]].

Art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible and readable when displayed. Typography involves selecting typefaces, point sizes, line lengths, line spacing and letter spacing. The term also describes the style and appearance of the letters, numbers and symbols so produced. It may also serve as an ornamental device unrelated to communicating information. Type design is a closely related craft, though most typographers do not design typefaces. Until the digital age it was a specialized occupation, but [[Personal computer|personal computers]] opened it to new designers and lay users. The word derives from Greek *týpos* (type) and *-graphía* (writing). Movable type was invented in the 11th-century [[Song dynasty]] of China by Bi Sheng, and metal movable type appeared in Korea during the [[Goryeo]] period, c. 1230.

American model, television personality and businesswoman. The first [[African Americans|African American]] woman on the cover of *GQ*, she was one of the few Black models to achieve supermodel status and was a Victoria's Secret Angel from 1997 to 2005. She created the reality series *America's Next Top Model*, which she hosted for its first 22 seasons. Her talk show, *The Tyra Banks Show* (2005–2010), on [[The CW]], won two Daytime Emmy awards. Her young adult novel *Modelland* topped *The New York Times* Best Seller list in 2011. Banks was repeatedly ranked among the world's most influential people by *Time*.
